A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAPD study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained content to be matched despite substantial reorganization and added experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original few-shot VQA experiments, component analyses, image-perturbation tests and computational measurements in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds LoRA comparisons, architecture experiments, attention analysis and compute-matched evaluations.

M1.justification: The attention mapper, learned soft prompts, frozen backbone components, two-stage training, first-order MAML updates and test-time adaptation procedure remain unchanged. Additional backbone configurations and component ablations test the existing method rather than introduce a revised MAPD algorithm.

E1.justification: The training mixture and four principal VL-ICL datasets remain unchanged. v3 Figure 2 adds text-to-text evaluation scenarios for Operator Induction and CLEVR Count Induction alongside their image-to-text versions, modestly extending input-condition coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds three LoRA configurations in Tables 2 and 12. Its Table 13 extends v1 Table 9 with Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and connector-finetuning variants of previously ICL-only public LLaVA comparators. The original prompt-distillation comparators remain.

E3.justification: New experiments vary language-model and vision-encoder configurations, LoRA placement and parameter budgets, and explicit task instructions. v3 also introduces normalized attention entropy and FLOPs-matched ICL-versus-FT evaluation. The original data splits and validation-based selection within 30 adaptation steps remain; newly disclosed meta-task counts do not establish changed sampling.

E4.justification: v3 adds modality comparisons, mapper-versus-MLP ablations with and without soft prompts, backbone-generalization tests, attention-entropy analysis and accuracy-versus-compute analysis. Its convergence plots also compare methods instead of only MAPD shot settings. The earlier perturbation and example-selection analyses are retained in Appendices A.2.7-A.2.8.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates, whereas v3 systematically adds 95% binomial confidence intervals to principal and model-comparison results in Tables 1-3 and 13. Neither PDF establishes repeated training runs or seed-based uncertainty; the intervals should not be interpreted as evidence of additional runs.

E6.justification: Original main scores are retained in v3 Table 11, while substantial new comparison and analysis results are added. In the retained high-shot FT experiment, In-ContextPD's Operator Induction scores change from 25.0/36.5/35.0 to 58.3/53.3/76.7 at 16/32/64 shots (v1 Table 6; v3 Table 16). These are revised reported values, not an established MAPD performance gain.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, MAPD objectives, first-order updates and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The added attention-analysis equations express standard probability normalization and Shannon entropy for an empirical metric; no substantive theoretical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion broaden the mapper's claimed applicability from LLaVA v1.5 to any LMM architecture. v3 also extends superiority claims to parameter-efficient finetuning, reporting a 7.7-point average advantage over its best LoRA configuration, and adds claims about favorable scaling with test-time compute.

C2.justification: v3 adds attention-based explanations for ICL degradation and interprets component ablations as evidence for visual-feature distillation. Its compute discussion now distinguishes low-budget ICL advantages from higher-budget FT advantages and identifies context-length constraints. Appendix A.2.5 newly qualifies public-model comparisons by architecture, scale and training-data differences.

D1.justification: v3 adds training and evaluation meta-task counts and compositions, expanded hyperparameter-search tables, detailed instruction prompts, LoRA target matrices, ranks, scaling factors and learning rates, plus hardware requirements for smaller models. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. The MAPD code-access link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: A dedicated Related Work section substantially expands positioning around prompt learning and test-time adaptation, adding works including PromptSRC, TPT and LoRA. It explicitly distinguishes MAPD's use of full visual patch features from Najdenkoska et al.'s CLS-token approach, beyond v1's shorter attribution.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the abstract and substantial introductory and experimental discussion, adds a Related Work section, reorganizes analyses around explicit questions and extensively restructures the appendix. Standalone limitations become concluding qualifications, while the Broader Impact section is removed.

P2.justification: The dense main results table becomes a compact summary, with detailed scores retained as appendix Table 11. Earlier robustness and selection displays move to the appendix. New modality, component and architecture displays are added, convergence plots are redrawn, and the original FLOPs-overhead plot is replaced by latency and compute-matched accuracy panels.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important evidential gaps in v1 through LoRA comparisons, direct component ablations, alternative-backbone tests and FLOPs-matched evaluation. Expanded sampling and hyperparameter documentation also makes the work substantially easier to assess and reproduce. Claims about applicability to any LMM and state-of-the-art performance remain broader than the demonstrated evidence, but the added controls and more qualified compute discussion provide a substantial net improvement.
